newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs seen steady-off $1 - private.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs seen steady-off $1 - private.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices Friday were seen steady to $1.00 per cwt lower, pressured by thin demand from packers planning light weekend slaughter, livestock dealers and packer buyers said.
Declines also were seen furthered by larger-than-expected hog marketings on Wednesday in some areas and projections for continued large marketings Thursday.
Interior Iowa/southern Minnesota hog receipts Wednesday came in at 112,000 head, well above the estimate of 100,000, USDA said. Receipts Thursday were estimated at 105,000 head.
Midwest cash hog prices rallied earlier in the week when extreme heat and humidity forced some farmers to limit movement to avoid potential increased stress and death loss, market sources said.
But cooler weather Wednesday encouraged increased marketings as did outlooks for lighter packer demand next week because of the Independence Day holiday Friday, sources said.

Interior Iowa/southern Minnesota top prices for hogs delivered to the plant were seen steady at $59.50 after declining from their peak on Tuesday at $61.00. Illinois top prices were seen at $58.00 to $58.50.
Indiana/Ohio top prices were expected $59.50 to $60.00.
